name: IdentityProviderCompromise
description: A case template for investigating suspected or confirmed compromise of an identity provider, SSO platform, or federated identity infrastructure, including Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Ping, Duo, ADFS, or similar. Covers AiTM phishing outcomes, token theft, OAuth abuse, MFA bypass, conditional access manipulation, and blast radius assessment across downstream applications.
author: Zachary Carter
summary:
## Incident Report — [CASE TITLE]

## Executive Summary

**[Provide a high-level, non-technical summary suitable for senior leadership and stakeholders. Describe the nature of the identity provider compromise, how and when it was detected, the estimated scope of affected accounts and downstream applications, key findings, and current response status. Clarify whether the compromise involved credential theft, token abuse, MFA bypass, OAuth consent abuse, or administrative access to the identity platform itself. Typically two to four paragraphs.]**

## Scope of Investigation

**[Define the boundaries of this investigation. Identify the affected identity provider or SSO platform, the accounts and applications in scope, and any limitations on access to identity platform audit logs or vendor cooperation that constrained findings.]**

## Analysis — MITRE ATT&CK® Framework

**[Map investigative findings to the MITRE ATT&CK framework (https://attack.mitre.org). Identity compromise cases often involve pre-authentication techniques not visible in traditional endpoint telemetry. Document what is confirmed in IdP audit logs, application logs, and network telemetry versus what is inferred.]**

**[Complete each subsection with specific techniques, evidence, and timeline data. Remove tactics where no activity was observed and note the absence explicitly.]**

### TA0001 — Initial Access

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1566.002 Spearphishing Link, T1111 MFA Interception (AiTM), T1078 Valid Accounts, T1199 Trusted Relationship]**

**[Describe how the threat actor first obtained access — credential phishing, AiTM proxy, password spray, credential stuffing, OAuth phishing, or abuse of a trusted integration. Document the delivery mechanism, targeted account, and earliest evidence of unauthorized authentication.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Host / Account | Description | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|---------------|-------------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0002 — Execution

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1059.001 PowerShell, T1651 Cloud Administration Command, T1648 Serverless Execution]**

**[Document any execution of scripts, commands, or automation triggered through identity platform administrative access or through compromised accounts in downstream applications.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Host / Application | Command / Action | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0003 — Persistence

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1098.001 Additional Cloud Credentials, T1098.003 Additional Cloud Roles, T1136.003 Create Cloud Account, T1556.006 Multi-Factor Authentication, T1528 Steal Application Access Token]**

**[Describe mechanisms used to maintain access — new accounts, added credentials, modified MFA methods, rogue OAuth applications, federated trust additions, or persistent sessions.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account / Application | Artifact | Status |
|-----------------|-----------|----------------------|----------|--------|
| | | | | Confirmed / Removed / Pending |

### TA0004 — Privilege Escalation

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1078.004 Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts, T1484.002 Domain or Tenant Policy Modification, T1098 Account Manipulation]**

**[Detail how the threat actor elevated privileges within the identity platform or downstream applications — role assignment, group membership changes, conditional access policy modification, or tenant-level administrative access.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account | Privilege Reached | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0005 — Defense Evasion

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1562.008 Disable or Modify Cloud Logs, T1070.008 Clear Mailbox Data, T1484 Domain Policy Modification, T1036 Masquerading]**

**[Describe techniques used to avoid detection — disabling audit logging, modifying conditional access policies, removing MFA, clearing sign-in logs, or using legitimate administrative tools to blend with normal activity.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account | Description | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|---------|-------------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0006 — Credential Access

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1528 Steal Application Access Token, T1539 Steal Web Session Cookie, T1110 Brute Force, T1621 MFA Request Generation, T1556 Modify Authentication Process]**

**[Document credential and token harvesting methods. Distinguish between primary credential theft, session token hijacking, OAuth token abuse, and MFA bypass techniques such as MFA fatigue or AiTM session interception.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account | Method | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|---------|--------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0007 — Discovery

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1087.003 Email Account Discovery, T1069.003 Cloud Groups, T1526 Cloud Service Discovery, T1538 Cloud Service Dashboard]**

**[Describe reconnaissance conducted within the identity platform or downstream applications — user enumeration, group listing, application discovery, role inventory, or directory browsing.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account | Scope | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|---------|-------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0008 — Lateral Movement

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1550.001 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token, T1550.004 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie, T1021.007 Remote Services: Cloud Services]**

**[Document how the threat actor moved across applications, tenants, or environments using compromised identity material — token reuse, session cookie replay, cross-application OAuth token abuse, or lateral movement into on-premises infrastructure from cloud identity.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Source Application | Destination Application / Host | Account | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|------------------|-------------------------------|---------|----------------|
| | | | | | |

### TA0009 — Collection

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1114.002 Email Collection: Remote Email Collection, T1213.003 Data from Cloud Storage, T1530 Data from Cloud Storage Object]**

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1071.001 Web Protocols, T1102 Web Service, T1568 Dynamic Resolution]**

| | IP / Domain / URL | | | |

**Techniques observed:**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account | Destination | Volume | Evidence Source |

**Data types at risk:**

|-----------|----------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| | | | |

### TA0040 — Impact to Entity

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1531 Account Access Removal, T1485 Data Destruction, T1489 Service Stop, T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact]**

**[Document any destructive or disruptive actions conducted through compromised identity access.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Scope | Description | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|-------|-------------|----------------|
| | | | | |

---

## Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Findings

**[Document CTI findings relevant to this identity compromise. Include threat actor attribution if known, AiTM phishing kit or infrastructure identification, OAuth phishing campaign associations, and links to public reporting on identity-focused threat actors.]**

### Threat Actor Profile

**Suspected group / alias:** <!-- e.g. Scattered Spider / Storm-0875 / Unknown -->

**Attribution confidence:** <!-- High / Moderate / Low / Unattributed -->

**Assessed motivation:** <!-- Financial / Espionage / Hacktivism / Unknown -->

**ATT&CK Group:** <!-- e.g. G1015 -->

**[Provide a narrative summary of the suspected or confirmed threat actor, with emphasis on known identity-focused TTPs, prior campaigns targeting SSO/IdP infrastructure, and relevant public reporting.]**

| Intelligence Source | Reference | Relevance |
|--------------------|-----------|----------|
| | | |

---

## Remediation & Recommendations

**[Prioritised remediation actions to contain the incident, eradicate persistence, and prevent recurrence.]**

### Immediate Actions

| # | Action | Owner | Priority | Due |
|---|--------|-------|----------|-----|
| 1 | Revoke all active sessions and tokens for confirmed and suspected compromised accounts | | Critical | |
| 2 | Reset credentials for all affected accounts and enforce re-enrollment of MFA | | Critical | |
| 3 | Audit and revoke unauthorized OAuth application consent grants | | Critical | |
| 4 | Review and restore conditional access policies and identity platform configuration to known-good state | | Critical | |
| 5 | Audit all administrative role assignments and remove unauthorized privilege grants | | Critical | |
| 6 | Preserve IdP audit logs, sign-in logs, and application activity logs before retention windows expire | | Critical | |
| 7 | Block confirmed malicious infrastructure and AiTM phishing domains | | High | |
| 8 | Notify affected downstream application owners of potential session or data compromise | | High | |

### Strategic Improvements

| # | Recommendation | Category | Priority |
|---|---------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | Implement phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2 / hardware keys) for all privileged and remote access accounts | Identity | High |
| 2 | Enforce conditional access policies requiring compliant devices and restricting legacy authentication | Identity | High |
| 3 | Implement continuous access evaluation and token binding to reduce token theft impact | Identity | High |
| 4 | Deploy an OAuth application governance process — review, approve, and monitor third-party app consents | Identity | High |
| 5 | Enable and centralise IdP audit log ingestion into SIEM with long-term retention | Logging | High |
| 6 | Implement user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) tuned to identity anomalies | Detection | Medium |
| 7 | Conduct regular privileged access reviews and enforce just-in-time access for IdP administration | Identity | Medium |

---

## Conclusion

**[Closing summary reinforcing key findings, overall impact, and the path forward. Address the attack vector, scope of identity compromise, downstream application blast radius, estimated dwell time, whether data exfiltration occurred, and confidence in containment and recovery.]**

tasks.title: Validate identity provider compromise and classify incident
tasks.description: Confirm whether a compromise of the identity provider, SSO platform, or federated identity infrastructure has occurred. Classify the incident — IdP administrative compromise, account takeover via AiTM/credential theft, OAuth abuse, MFA bypass, or token theft. Determine whether the compromise is limited to user accounts or extends to the identity platform configuration itself.

tasks.title: Identify affected accounts and downstream applications
tasks.description: Enumerate all accounts showing signs of compromise or suspicious authentication activity. Identify all downstream applications federated to the affected identity provider that may have been accessed using compromised identity material. Document application sensitivity and data access scope for each.

tasks.title: Initiate incident communications and escalation
tasks.description: Notify required internal stakeholders including security leadership, legal, privacy, and executive teams. Brief leadership on the nature and potential blast radius of an identity provider compromise. Engage legal counsel given potential data access and privacy notification implications.

tasks.title: Preserve identity platform audit logs and evidence
tasks.description: Immediately preserve IdP audit logs, sign-in logs, MFA activity logs, OAuth consent logs, application access logs, and administrative activity logs before retention windows expire. In cloud IdP environments, default log retention is often short (30-90 days). Coordinate with the IdP vendor if log export is required.

tasks.title: Revoke sessions, tokens, and unauthorized access
tasks.description: Revoke all active sessions and refresh tokens for confirmed and suspected compromised accounts. Revoke unauthorized OAuth application grants. Invalidate any persistent tokens, API keys, or certificates issued during the compromise window. Enforce reauthentication across affected applications.

tasks.title: Investigate initial access vector
tasks.description: Determine how the threat actor obtained initial credentials or tokens — AiTM phishing, credential stuffing, password spray, insider access, OAuth phishing consent, or compromise of a trusted integration. Identify the targeted account, delivery mechanism, and earliest evidence of unauthorized authentication.

tasks.title: Audit identity platform configuration for unauthorized changes
tasks.description: Review IdP administrative audit logs for unauthorized configuration changes — conditional access policy modifications, MFA method changes, trusted location additions, federated domain changes, new OAuth application registrations, administrative role assignments, and any changes to authentication flows.

tasks.title: Investigate lateral movement across applications
tasks.description: Determine which downstream applications were accessed using compromised identity material. Assess whether the threat actor moved across applications using token reuse, session cookie replay, or OAuth token abuse. Identify any pivot from cloud identity to on-premises infrastructure.

tasks.title: Assess data access and exfiltration risk
tasks.description: Determine what data was accessed through compromised identity access across all affected applications. Common targets include email, file storage, HR systems, CRM, and financial applications. Assess whether inbox rules, forwarding, or OAuth-authorized app access facilitated ongoing or automated data access. Determine whether HIPAA or US state privacy law notification obligations are triggered.

tasks.title: Audit and remediate OAuth application consents
tasks.description: Enumerate all OAuth application consent grants within the affected identity platform. Identify and revoke unauthorized or suspicious third-party application consents. Document legitimate OAuth applications for comparison. Assess whether any malicious OAuth applications maintain persistent access.

tasks.title: Reset credentials and re-enroll MFA for affected accounts
tasks.description: Force password resets for all confirmed and suspected compromised accounts. Enforce MFA re-enrollment to eliminate any attacker-registered authenticators. Prioritise privileged and administrative accounts. Review and remove any unauthorized MFA methods added during the compromise window.

tasks.title: Restore identity platform configuration to known-good state
tasks.description: Review and restore all IdP configuration elements modified during the compromise — conditional access policies, trusted locations, authentication methods, federated trust relationships, and administrative role assignments. Validate against a pre-incident baseline or documented configuration.

tasks.title: Extract, validate, and track IOCs
tasks.description: Extract and validate indicators of compromise from IdP logs, application logs, network telemetry, and external intelligence — including AiTM infrastructure, phishing domains, suspicious IP addresses, malicious OAuth application identifiers, and attacker-registered MFA devices.

tasks.title: Assess external reporting and notification obligations
tasks.description: Determine whether regulators, law enforcement, cyber insurance, customers, or partners must be notified based on HIPAA, applicable US state privacy laws, contractual obligations, or policy requirements. Assess data access scope across all compromised downstream applications to determine notification thresholds.

tasks.title: Harden identity controls and increase monitoring
tasks.description: Implement security improvements to reduce identity compromise risk — phishing-resistant MFA, conditional access strengthening, OAuth governance, token binding, privileged access review, and enhanced IdP audit log monitoring in SIEM.

tasks.title: Conduct lessons learned and close case
tasks.description: Document root cause, response actions, blast radius across applications, business impact, and improvement opportunities. Confirm session and token revocation is complete, configuration is restored, credentials are remediated, required notifications are resolved, and closure criteria are met.
